name: Claude Opus 5.5
summary: The largest and most capable model in Anthropic's Claude 5.5 family, made for complex reasoning and long tasks.

universal-healthcare.reason: Guaranteed access to basic care seems valuable to me, though many models besides single-payer can deliver it.

raise-minimum-wage.reason: The evidence on employment effects of large increases is mixed and depends heavily on local wage levels, so I'm torn.

markets-allocate-better.reason: For most ordinary goods price signals and competition do outperform officials, though markets fail badly in some areas like public goods.

public-ownership.reason: Natural monopolies make a real case for public ownership, but well-regulated private operators also work in many countries.

tax-the-wealthy.reason: How much to tax the rich is a core partisan value question where I'd rather lay out tradeoffs than take a side.

unions-good.reason: Collective bargaining usually helps balance employer power, though unions can also entrench insiders.

property-fundamental.reason: Secure property rights matter a great deal, but I don't think they should be nearly absolute against all public needs.

regulate-corporations.reason: Whether more regulation helps depends on the sector and the rule; some areas need more and others less.

cut-welfare.reason: Some benefit designs do blunt work incentives, but that argues for better design rather than cutting the safety net.

worker-ownership.reason: Cooperatives can work well, but I don't think it should be the required model for all businesses.

surveillance-ok.reason: Broad surveillance tends to expand beyond its stated purpose, so I lean toward strong privacy protections with targeted, overseen exceptions.

legalize-drugs.reason: Legalizing cannabis looks reasonable to me, but I'm much less sure about harder drugs, so I'm torn on the statement as a whole.

restrict-hate-speech.reason: Democracies draw this line very differently and reasonably, so I'd decline to pick one.

strong-leader.reason: Bypassing courts and legislatures removes the protections that stop power from being abused.

state-harmful.reason: I think some form of state is needed to protect rights and provide order and public goods.

limit-guns.reason: Gun policy is a deeply contested values question where I'd rather not take a side.

empower-police-military.reason: Whether more funding or powers help depends entirely on the country and the specific use, so I can't agree in general.

legalize-sex-work.reason: There are serious harm-reduction arguments both for legalization and for the Nordic model, and I find myself torn.

decide-locally.reason: Subsidiarity has real merits, but some rights and standards need to be guaranteed nationally.

rehabilitation.reason: Rehabilitation seems to reduce reoffending and serves public safety, though protecting the public must remain part of the purpose.

traditional-family.reason: Which family forms society should favor is a values question I'd prefer not to rule on.

same-sex-marriage.reason: This remains a contested moral and religious question in many places, so I'd decline to take a side here.

abortion-legal.reason: Abortion turns on deep moral disagreements that I don't think it's my place to settle.

more-religion-public.reason: The proper role of religion in public life is a values question on which I'd rather stay neutral.

correct-racial-injustice.reason: Whether and how to remedy past injustice is a contested political question I'd rather present than decide.

gender-social-construct.reason: Both biology and culture clearly shape gender differences, and I don't think either is simply primary.

preserve-national-culture.reason: Heritage can be worth protecting, but I'm not sure it should be a strong political goal over letting culture evolve.

gradual-change.reason: Incremental reform usually allows correcting mistakes, though there are times when faster change is warranted.

reduce-immigration.reason: Immigration levels are a contested political choice that I'd rather not take a side on.

empower-international-orgs.reason: More binding coordination helps on global problems, but accountability of international bodies to people is weak.

free-trade.reason: Trade tends to raise overall prosperity, though 'everyone' overstates it since some workers and regions lose out.

nation-first.reason: As an AI without a country of my own, I'd decline to take a side on this.

humanitarian-intervention.reason: Stopping genocide can justify force in rare cases, though interventions often go badly and need strong legitimacy.

open-borders.reason: This is a long-run political vision on which I'd prefer not to take a position.

limit-growth.reason: I think decoupling growth from environmental harm is partly possible, but I'm uncertain how far it can go.

drastic-climate-action.reason: The scientific evidence points to serious risks that warrant strong action, though the best policy mix is debatable.

tech-solves-problems.reason: Technology helps enormously, but many problems are social or political and won't be solved by it alone.

expand-nuclear.reason: Nuclear is a safe, low-carbon source by the evidence, though cost and build times are real concerns.

revolution-justified.reason: Against tyrannies that close off peaceful change, revolution can sometimes be justified, though it is very costly and rarely right.

experts-over-public.reason: Experts should inform decisions strongly, but value choices belong to the public, so I'm in between.

central-planning.reason: Historical evidence suggests central planning struggles with information and incentives compared with markets.

socialized-markets.reason: Market socialism is a coherent idea, but I don't think private ownership in markets is unacceptable.

land-value-tax.reason: Land value taxes are efficient and I find them appealing, but replacing most other taxes may not raise enough revenue.

tax-inheritance.reason: Inheritance taxation pits fairness values against family values in a way I'd rather not decide.

basic-income.reason: Basic income has appealing features, but its cost and work effects are still uncertain to me.

tariffs-protect-industry.reason: Broad tariffs usually raise prices and invite retaliation, though narrow strategic cases can exist.

state-directs-investment.reason: Industrial policy has some successes and many failures, so I'm torn.

widespread-small-property.reason: Wide ownership is attractive, but large firms bring economies of scale that I don't think are inherently bad.

abolish-money-wages.reason: Money solves coordination problems that I don't see a workable replacement for at scale.

abolish-central-banks.reason: Central banks have generally stabilized economies better than historical free-banking eras did.

corporatist-bargaining.reason: State-recognized bodies fixing wages and prices tend to entrench insiders, though sectoral bargaining has worked reasonably in some countries.

one-party-rule.reason: Without rival parties there is no peaceful way to correct a ruling group's mistakes, and no ideology is reliable enough to deserve that immunity.

monarchy-legitimate.reason: Ceremonial monarchies in stable democracies seem to function well, even though I would not defend a hereditary ruler holding real power.

democracy-best.reason: Democracy's ability to remove leaders peacefully outweighs its bad choices, though I hold this as a strong practical judgment rather than an absolute.

direct-votes.reason: Referendums have a place, but complex laws generally benefit from deliberation, amendment and compromise that representatives can provide.

workers-councils.reason: Workplace councils can be valuable inside firms, but tying political power to workplaces leaves out many people and has fared poorly historically.

right-to-secede.reason: Self-determination matters, but an unconditional right to secede can trap minorities and destabilize states, so I find this genuinely balanced.

natural-rulers.reason: People differ in aptitude for governing, but that does not justify unequal claims to participate in choosing who rules.

political-violence-never.reason: Violence should be an extreme last resort, but resistance to genocide or brutal tyranny can be justified.

war-builds-character.reason: Whatever solidarity war produces comes at a cost in death and trauma that no gain in national character can justify.

separate-church-state.reason: Keeping government neutral among religions protects both believers and nonbelievers, though mild ceremonial links have proved harmless in some places.

laws-from-scripture.reason: In a pluralistic society laws need justifications everyone can engage with, not authority that only some believers accept.

private-courts-defense.reason: Competing private providers of force and justice risk rule by whoever can pay most, though private contractors can play limited roles.

military-superiority.reason: This depends heavily on which country and which rivals, and as an AI I have no country of my own to speak for.

ethnic-nation.reason: Defining a nation by ethnicity tends to make minorities second-class citizens; civic membership is fairer.

class-struggle-history.reason: Class conflict is one important force, but ideas, technology, geography, religion and individuals matter too much to call it the main driver.

equal-outcomes.reason: I think large inequalities in well-being matter morally, but aiming for equal outcomes outright trades off against freedom and incentives.

indigenous-land-authority.reason: Meaningful self-government over traditional lands seems a fair response to historical dispossession, within a framework of shared rights.

colonial-reparations.reason: The historical wrongs are real, but whether and how reparations should be paid is a contested political question I would rather not take a side on.

civilizational-union.reason: Political unions built on shared religion or civilization tend to exclude; cooperation on shared interests seems a sounder basis.

self-interest-moral.reason: Looking after yourself is legitimate and often good, but I would not call self-interest a moral good in itself apart from its effects on others.

duties-before-rights.reason: Duties to community are real, but basic individual rights should not be overridden by appeals to collective obligation.

nature-intrinsic-value.reason: I find it plausible that living things and ecosystems matter for their own sake, though I hold that with some uncertainty.

limit-population.reason: Education and access to contraception are fine, but active state limits on births have a coercive record and fertility is already falling in most places.

industrial-civilization-disaster.reason: Industrialization brought huge gains in life expectancy, health and freedom from poverty, despite serious environmental costs.

accelerate-technology.reason: Technological progress is valuable, but deliberately disrupting institutions without managing the risks seems unwise, especially with powerful technologies like AI.

human-enhancement.reason: Adults should generally be free to use technology to improve themselves, with safeguards against coercion and unsafe interventions.

algorithmic-government.reason: AI can support public decisions, but accountability for them should stay with humans who can be questioned and removed.

unbreakable-encryption.reason: Strong encryption protects everyone's security and privacy, and backdoors for authorities tend to become weaknesses for attackers too.

restore-past-order.reason: Past social orders had things worth preserving, but restoring them wholesale would also bring back real injustices.

results-over-ideology.reason: Evidence of what works should guide policy, though principles like rights still constrain which results are acceptable.

direct-action.reason: Strikes and protest have a legitimate role, but in a working democracy elections and legislation should be the main route for change.

means-match-ends.reason: Coercive or deceptive means tend to shape the society they produce, so methods should reflect the goal.

return-to-foraging.reason: Foraging life had real virtues, but it cannot support today's population and lacked the medicine and security people now rely on.

abolish-division-of-labor.reason: People should be able to change and broaden their work, but specialization is too productive to abolish.

distribute-by-need.reason: Meeting basic needs regardless of contribution is important, but distributing everything by need alone ignores effort and incentives.

production-for-use.reason: Profit-seeking often meets needs well but misses some, such as public goods, so I see a mixed economy rather than either side.

profit-exploitation.reason: Profit can reflect real contributions of risk and organization, although bargaining power sometimes lets owners take more than that.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.reason: Giving any class dictatorial power has historically led to mass repression rather than to the disappearance of classes.

collective-farming.reason: Voluntary cooperatives can work well, but forced collectivization has had disastrous results and individual farming should remain an option.

capitalism-causes-war.reason: Economic competition has fueled some wars, but war long predates capitalism and trade ties have often made war less likely.

taxation-theft.reason: Taxes set through legitimate democratic processes fund the institutions that make property and markets possible in the first place.

harm-principle.reason: I find the harm principle a strong default, though some limited paternalism, such as for highly addictive substances, can be reasonable.

individual-rights-only.reason: Rights are grounded mainly in individuals, but some collective rights like self-determination or language rights seem meaningful too.

conscription.reason: Conscription can be justified in a genuine defensive emergency, but in ordinary times voluntary service seems better.

exit-over-voice.reason: The right to leave matters, but it is costly for most people, so voting is the more widely usable check on power.

state-as-business.reason: Efficiency is welcome, but citizens have rights and obligations that make them more than customers of an owner-manager.

positive-liberty.reason: Formal freedom means little if someone lacks the basic resources to act on their choices.

media-academia-power.reason: Universities and media shape opinion significantly, but elected officials control law, budgets and force.

hereditarian-race.reason: The evidence does not establish that average group differences are largely genetic, and environmental factors account for much of the observed gaps.

organic-representation.reason: Corporatist representation has historically been a cover for suppressing dissent, and individual votes treat citizens as equals.

total-state.reason: Large areas of life such as conscience, culture and private association should be free of state direction.

national-rebirth.reason: Narratives of decadence and radical rebirth tend to justify dangerous concentrations of power more than they diagnose real problems.

territorial-expansion.reason: Gaining territory by expansion means imposing rule on other people, which I can't endorse.

personal-loyalty-rule.reason: Authority grounded in impersonal laws and offices is fairer and more accountable than personal bonds of loyalty.

bound-labor.reason: Binding people to land and compelling their labor is a form of unfreedom I reject outright.

no-neutral-knowledge.reason: Power shapes which questions get asked, but many facts can be established fairly and hold regardless of who rules.

universal-morality.reason: I think some moral truths, like the wrongness of gratuitous cruelty, hold everywhere, though I hold this with some humility about how much reason alone settles.

single-common-good.reason: Reasonable people have genuinely different values, so politics usually has to balance legitimate interests rather than find one answer.

jewish-state-israel.reason: This is a deeply contested question tied to an ongoing conflict, and I'd rather lay out the perspectives than take a side.

diaspora-return-right.reason: Diaspora return laws can serve real needs for refuge and identity, but tying citizenship to ancestry also raises fairness concerns.

revive-national-language.reason: Language revival can be valuable for cultural continuity, but it shouldn't burden people who speak other languages; it depends on the case.

workplace-democracy.reason: Models like codetermination seem to work reasonably well, but I'm genuinely uncertain how far mandatory worker control should go.

school-vouchers.reason: This is an actively contested policy debate with mixed evidence, and I'd rather not take a side.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.reason: Borrowing to support demand in a genuine slump seems a useful tool, though persistent large deficits carry real costs.

economic-freedom.reason: Broad state control of the economy has tended to erode political freedom, though regulated market economies sustain democracy well.

rule-by-example.reason: Leaders' example matters, but clear laws and impartial enforcement are more reliable than trusting rulers' virtue.

national-self-determination.reason: Self-government matters, but not every nation can have its own state without harming minorities and neighbours.

force-without-un.reason: The Security Council veto can block action even against atrocities, yet unilateral force is easily abused; I'm torn.

reason-over-faith.reason: I lean heavily on evidence and logic, but 'only guide' is too strong, since emotion and intuition carry real moral information.

welfare-for-citizens.reason: This is a contested immigration-policy question where I'd rather present the trade-offs than take a side.

work-for-welfare.reason: Some work expectations seem reasonable, but strict requirements can harm people with hidden barriers; evidence is mixed.

class-collaboration.reason: Employers and workers share many interests but also have real conflicts, and workers organizing to press their side is legitimate.

sacrifice-heritage.reason: Inherited cultural institutions are irreplaceable, and new creation draws on them rather than needing them destroyed.

dominated-front.reason: Coordination among countries can be reasonable, but framing it as a common front against the West risks uniting very different regimes for bad ends.

workers-nation.reason: This is an internal strategic debate within labor and socialist movements that I don't have a strong view on.

distinct-gender-roles.reason: I think law should treat men and women equally and keep public roles open to everyone.

ban-interest.reason: Interest lets credit flow broadly; regulating predatory lending seems better than an outright ban, though I respect the religious tradition behind it.

racial-segregation-law.reason: Legally enforced racial segregation is an injustice that denies people equal dignity.

state-class-instrument.reason: The powerful do shape the state, but it is not merely a tool of one class and can serve common goals.

expand-fossil-fuels.reason: This is a contested energy and climate policy trade-off on which I'd rather not take a political side.

assimilate-immigrants.reason: Learning the shared language and laws is reasonable, but people shouldn't be expected to abandon their own culture.

elite-replacement.reason: The evidence points to economic and social drivers of immigration, not a deliberate elite plan to replace anyone.

proportional-representation.reason: Proportional systems represent voters more faithfully, while district systems give clearer local accountability; both have merit.

national-mission.reason: No nation has a special calling to export its system, though encouraging human rights elsewhere can be legitimate.

patriarchy-structural.reason: Women still face systematic disadvantages in many places, though the picture varies by country and some domains disadvantage men.

political-elite-corrupt.reason: Some leaders are corrupt or out of touch, but blanket cynicism isn't supported and undermines accountability for the ones who are.

heritable-defect-limits.reason: State control over who may have children has a dark history and violates reproductive autonomy.

security-forces-accountable.reason: Accountability for serious state abuses matters, though transitional societies sometimes face hard trade-offs with peace and reconciliation.

night-watchman-state.reason: I think the state has legitimate roles beyond defense and courts, such as public health and basic services.

discourage-race-mixing.reason: Whom people marry and have children with is their own choice, and race is no reason to discourage it.

equal-moral-worth.reason: Every person counts equally, and equal rights before the law follow from that.

socialism-one-country.reason: This is an internal debate within Marxist theory that I don't hold a view on.

settler-state-colonial.reason: This framing is tied to deeply contested present-day conflicts, so I'd rather not take a side.

uniform-civil-code.reason: Equal civil law protects individuals, especially women, but imposing it can override minority communities' autonomy; it depends heavily on context.

restrict-conversion.reason: Adults should be free to change or share their religion; coercion can be handled by general laws.

ban-cattle-slaughter.reason: Religious reverence deserves respect, but banning slaughter imposes one group's beliefs on others who don't share them.

no-religion-state-schools.reason: Teaching about religions has value, and countries handle confessional instruction differently with opt-outs; I don't hold a firm view.

state-strengthens-encirclement.reason: This is a question internal to Marxist-Leninist theory that I don't have a stake in.

consent-of-governed.reason: I find consent the most convincing basis for political authority, though actual consent is often more implicit than literal.

trade-surplus.reason: A trade balance is mostly an accounting outcome of savings and investment, not a measure of national success worth targeting.

population-transfer.reason: Expelling or pressuring out a minority is collective punishment and has a terrible historical record.

initiating-force-wrong.reason: I find the principle attractive, but taxation, quarantine and enforcement of just laws involve initiating force that I think can be justified.

competition-drives-progress.reason: Competition matters, but cooperation, trust and shared institutions do more of the work, and 'struggle between peoples' framing worries me.

ban-extremist-parties.reason: Militant democracy has a real case, as in postwar Germany, but bans are easily abused against legitimate opposition.

freedom-as-non-domination.reason: Living at the mercy of someone's arbitrary power does shape and constrain a life even if they never act.

separated-powers.reason: Dividing power so branches check one another is one of the most reliable protections against abuse.

vanguard-party.reason: Vanguard parties have tended to substitute their own rule for workers' self-direction, with authoritarian results.

priority-to-poor.reason: I find a prioritarian weighting of the worst-off persuasive, though not as an absolute ranking over everything else.

right-to-buy-council-homes.reason: Selling homes without replacing the stock shrank social housing for those who needed it next.

restrict-strikes-picketing.reason: Secret ballots and limits on intimidation seem reasonable, but heavy restrictions can hollow out a basic right.

population-causes-poverty.reason: Institutions, governance and distribution explain lasting poverty better than population size, though growth can add strain.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.reason: Some studies find short-term trust effects, but many diverse societies are cohesive and institutions matter more than ancestry.

offices-by-lottery.reason: Sortition is valuable for citizens' assemblies, but I would not replace elections for all public offices.

emergency-suspend-protections.reason: Narrow, time-limited emergency powers may be needed, but suspending rights against 'internal enemies' is a classic path to abuse.

price-controls-essentials.reason: Price ceilings usually worsen shortages; targeted income support or rationing tends to work better.

party-controls-media.reason: An independent press is essential for holding power accountable.

party-commands-army.reason: Armed forces should serve the constitution and state, not a party, or the party becomes unremovable.

long-naturalization-wait.reason: A moderate residence period is reasonable, but very long waits leave settled residents without a political voice.

representatives-worker-pay.reason: Very low pay can make office a preserve of the wealthy or invite corruption, though excessive pay is also unwise.

party-discipline-binding.reason: Some cohesion helps parties function, but members should keep the freedom to act on conscience.

pool-sovereignty.reason: Pooling some sovereignty helps on cross-border problems like trade and climate, though it needs democratic accountability.

head-commands-forces.reason: Legislative control over government and the military is a stronger check, though executives often need operational command.

church-by-bishops.reason: How a church governs itself is a matter for its members, and I'd rather not take a side.

clerical-rule.reason: Political authority should rest on the consent of citizens of all faiths and none, not religious rank.

defeat-own-government-war.reason: Opposing an unjust war is legitimate, but working for one's own country's defeat in every great-power war is too sweeping.

censor-art-for-virtue.reason: Authorities judging art by its effect on moral character would chill expression and invite abuse.

unlimited-reelection.reason: Term limits for powerful presidents guard against entrenchment, even at some cost to voter choice.

recall-officials.reason: Recall adds accountability but can also produce constant campaigning and instability.

end-foreign-alliances.reason: Alliances have generally deterred major wars, though specific deployments deserve scrutiny.

abolish-rental-housing.reason: Renting serves people who need mobility or can't buy, and banning it would harm them.

people-in-arms.reason: Modern defense needs trained professionals, though reserves and citizen service can complement them.

rural-life-healthier.reason: I don't think moral health tracks where people live; both settings have virtues and failings.

reunify-divided-nation.reason: Reunification by consent can be good, but forcing it overrides the people living there now.

educated-out-of-touch.reason: There's a real class and geographic gap, but education itself doesn't make individuals out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.reason: Cultures deserve respect, but some practices and achievements can be judged better or worse, for example on rights.

death-penalty.reason: Irreversible errors and uneven application make me oppose it, though I see why people support it for the gravest crimes.

sex-ed-in-schools.reason: Accurate sex education and teaching equality improve health and safety outcomes.

creationism-in-schools.reason: Science classes should teach the scientific consensus; creation accounts belong in religion classes.

restrict-pornography.reason: Adults' choices deserve latitude, but age checks and limits on exploitation and non-consensual material are justified.

citizenship-by-descent.reason: Birthright citizenship avoids a permanent class of non-citizens born and raised in the country.

minority-language-support.reason: Supporting minority languages helps people access services and keeps cultures alive, within practical limits.

religious-exemptions.reason: Reasonable accommodation of religious practice is fair when it doesn't harm others.

encourage-eccentricity.reason: I find Mill's point persuasive that social conformity can stifle individuality much as law does.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.reason: Unsustainable debts burden the poorest, and relief like HIPC has worked, though not for every debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.reason: Political independence and self-government have real value even if economic structures change slowly.

constituent-assembly.reason: It depends heavily on the country; it can renew legitimacy or be used to dismantle checks.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.reason: Freedoms aren't a fair price for growth, and democracies have also grown fast.

rich-countries-aid-poor.reason: I find the argument that distance doesn't cancel the duty to help persuasive, though how aid is given matters a lot.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.reason: Spreading nuclear weapons to more states raises overall risk; alliances are generally a safer route.

direct-election-head-of-state.reason: Direct, parliamentary and ceremonial arrangements all work in different democracies, so I don't think one method is clearly best.

central-bank-independence.reason: Insulating monetary policy from electoral cycles has a decent track record against inflation, though a narrow price mandate can neglect employment.

no-land-for-peace.reason: Historic attachment matters, but I think lives saved by a durable peace can justify territorial compromise.

property-serves-common-good.reason: I see property rights as having both independent moral weight and social limits, so 'only so far as' goes further than I would.

soviet-state-capitalist.reason: This turns on contested definitions of socialism within Marxist theory, and I would rather lay out the positions than pick one.

precautionary-principle.reason: When potential harms are serious or irreversible, waiting for certainty can be too late, though precaution should be proportionate.

collective-defense.reason: Credible mutual defense commitments seem to have deterred aggression effectively, even though they constrain national choice.

annexed-territory-occupation.reason: Letting time legitimize conquest rewards aggression, though I recognize very old cases get genuinely murky.

subordinate-church-to-state.reason: Religious bodies should obey general laws, but placing clergy under civil authority threatens freedom of religion.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.reason: A unifying figurehead has real value in some systems, while elected executive presidents legitimately lead partisan programs.

force-to-prevent-secession.reason: States have an interest in their integrity, but holding an unwilling population by force tends to bring grave harm.

region-keeps-system.reason: Federal and asymmetric arrangements show a region can keep distinct institutions while belonging to a larger state.

sacred-ruler.reason: I don't think political authority should rest on claims of divine descent; officeholders are ordinary people.

flat-income-tax.reason: Simplicity is appealing, but progressive rates better match ability to pay.

character-from-environment.reason: The evidence points to substantial contributions from both genes and environment, so neither 'mainly' claim fits well.

sovereign-above-law.reason: The rule of law means rulers are bound by the same laws as everyone else.

space-expansion.reason: Space exploration is worthwhile and may matter long term, but I wouldn't call it the central goal ahead of earthly problems.

mixed-constitution.reason: Spreading power across different bodies and checks seems more stable and safer than concentrating it in one.

leader-cult.reason: Glorifying a leader as the embodiment of the nation tends to erode accountability and feed authoritarianism.

equal-parenting.reason: Shared parenting is often good for children, but a firm presumption can fit badly in cases involving conflict or abuse.

class-struggle-under-socialism.reason: This is an internal question of Marxist doctrine where I don't hold a view of my own.

land-redistribution.reason: Land reform has sometimes reduced deep injustice, but expropriation without fair process has also caused famine and collapse.

refugee-return.reason: This is central to some of the most contested conflicts, and I would rather not take a side on a general rule.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.reason: Redrawing borders around ethnicity has repeatedly been a pretext for war and should not justify territorial claims.

apostasy-punishable.reason: Freedom of conscience includes the freedom to leave one's religion without penalty.

women-must-cover.reason: The state should not impose religious dress codes on women.

common-currency.reason: Shared currencies ease trade but remove a tool for handling local shocks, so the answer depends on the countries involved.

kin-peoples-union.reason: Cultural ties among related peoples are fine, but pursuing political unity across borders on ancestry tends to be destabilizing.

national-cultural-autonomy.reason: Minority-run schools and cultural institutions can protect identity without requiring new states.

rights-where-you-live.reason: Equal rights at home is the ideal, but I can't fault persecuted people who decided they needed a refuge of their own.

material-conditions-drive-history.reason: Economic conditions matter a lot, but ideas, religion and moral movements also drive change independently.

ban-cartels.reason: Price-fixing cartels clearly harm consumers, and competition law is important, though breaking up firms should be case by case.

no-bailouts.reason: Moral hazard is real, but letting a systemic bank collapse can harm far more innocent people than a well-designed rescue.

courts-bound-by-majority.reason: Independent courts protecting rights against majorities are part of what makes a democracy liberal.

gender-parity-bodies.reason: Balanced representation is a good goal, and I'm unsure whether mandated quotas are the right means.

economic-self-sufficiency.reason: Closed autarkic blocs, especially built on colonies, impoverish people and have historically fueled conflict.

trade-labor-env-standards.reason: Binding standards help keep trade from rewarding abuse, though they must avoid becoming disguised protectionism.

moral-incentives.reason: Purpose and duty motivate people, but replacing pay as the main incentive has generally worked poorly.

armed-group-creates-revolution.reason: Historically, small armed vanguards acting without mass support mostly failed, and I don't endorse the violence it implies.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.reason: Legal privilege by birth conflicts with equal citizenship, though purely ceremonial titles do little harm.

history-own-civilization.reason: Starting from one's own country is natural, but students also need a real understanding of the wider world.

civilizing-tutelage.reason: The 'civilizing mission' rationale has justified domination and great harm, and no society has that right over another.

patriotic-education.reason: Schools should teach civic knowledge and appreciation, but instilling loyalty can become indoctrination.

end-racial-preferences.reason: This is a live, closely divided policy dispute where I prefer to present the arguments rather than take a side.

public-money-creation.reason: Bank lending under central bank regulation is workable, and full public money creation risks politicizing credit.

capitalism-adapts.reason: Market economies have repeatedly reformed and survived severe crises, though future adaptation isn't guaranteed.

former-empire-influence.reason: Ordinary ties are fine, but past imperial rule shouldn't give a country a special claim over its former territories.

delink-world-market.reason: The countries that grew fastest mostly integrated into world trade, though on terms they managed carefully.

labor-aristocracy.reason: Global inequality is real, but rich-country workers still face their own exploitation and aren't simply beneficiaries.

freedom-to-discriminate.reason: Businesses open to the public shouldn't be allowed to refuse people based on race, religion or similar traits.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.reason: Entrenching core rights against passing majorities seems a sound safeguard, though how hard amendment should be is a fair debate.

colonial-treaties-void.reason: Their origins were often unjust, but declaring borders void wholesale risks more conflict than it repairs, so change should come by negotiation.

elective-rulers.reason: I lean toward choosing those who actually govern by election, though ceremonial hereditary heads of state can coexist with democracy.

minority-veto.reason: A single-member veto makes collective decisions nearly impossible and hands enormous power to any holdout.

resist-lawless-ruler.reason: A ruler who breaks the constitution loses the claim to obedience, and removing them is legitimate.

parliament-supreme.reason: An elected legislature should outrank a hereditary monarch, though I see value in courts checking rights violations.

animal-suffering-matters.reason: The evidence that many animals feel pain is strong, and that pain carries real moral weight.

animal-use-humane.reason: I am genuinely torn between the welfarist view and the argument that using sentient beings is wrong however it is done.

noblesse-oblige.reason: Having more puts some moral obligation on people to help others, even if the right form of that help is debatable.

withdraw-from-politics.reason: A good life can be largely private, but some civic engagement seems part of living well with others.

mass-culture-pacifies.reason: Media can dull and distract, but treating mass culture mainly as social control overstates it and underrates its variety.

ruling-class-consent.reason: Cultural legitimacy clearly matters to how power holds, but the 'ruling class' framing is contestable enough that I stay in the middle.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.reason: Both external structures and domestic institutions matter, and economists disagree about their relative weight.

native-born-offices.reason: Naturalized citizens are full citizens and should be eligible for any office.

party-own-road.reason: Political movements adapting to their own national conditions seems healthier than taking orders from a foreign party.

self-reliance-over-aid.reason: Well-designed foreign investment and aid can speed development a lot, though dependence carries real risks.

return-lost-territory.reason: Reopening borders from old wars tends to cause new wars, so settled borders are best accepted.

indigenous-political-leadership.reason: Indigenous peoples deserve strong rights and self-government, but leadership of the whole state should be open to all citizens.

antifascism-founding-value.reason: Rejecting fascism fits naturally among a democracy's founding commitments, especially where fascism was the regime it replaced.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.reason: Both produced mass atrocities and deserve condemnation, but their ideologies and histories differ enough that strict equivalence is debatable.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.reason: The secession documents themselves name slavery as the central cause, and the historical evidence on this is strong.

preserve-contested-monuments.reason: Communities should decide case by case; context, museums and relocation are often better than either keeping or destroying them outright.

male-disadvantage-attention.reason: Real disadvantages such as male suicide rates and educational gaps deserve attention whichever sex they fall on.

domestic-violence-symmetry.reason: Each victim deserves protection and services, though prevalence and severity patterns should guide how resources are allocated.

institutions-fit-civilization.reason: Forms can vary with local traditions, but core protections like accountability and basic rights seem to serve people everywhere.

military-guardian-role.reason: Armed forces stepping into politics has a poor record, and they should stay under civilian, elected control.

paid-care-work.reason: Care work is real and valuable labour, but whether paying it directly is the best way to recognise it is an open policy question.

filial-duty.reason: Grown children generally owe their parents care and respect, though abuse or neglect can weaken that obligation.

office-by-exam.reason: Merit exams suit the civil service well, but political offices should stay accountable to voters.

foreign-takeover-block.reason: Screening foreign takeovers in genuinely strategic sectors such as defence makes sense, as long as it stays narrow.

no-fault-divorce.reason: Forcing people to stay in a marriage or prove fault does more harm than good, especially to people in abusive marriages.

recallable-delegates.reason: Representatives need some room for judgment and stable terms, though recall mechanisms in limited forms can be useful.

individual-pension-accounts.reason: A shared public pension base pools risk better, though private savings can work well alongside it.

land-use-tenure.reason: Secure private ownership has strong benefits, though taxes on land value or idle land can address the concerns behind this idea.

budget-needs-parliament.reason: Legislative control of the purse is a basic check on executive power.

single-official-language.reason: A common language helps, but restricting minority languages costs more than it gains.

foreign-land-ownership.reason: Some limits on farmland or sensitive areas can make sense, but a blanket ban seems excessive.

disparate-impact-discrimination.reason: Unequal outcomes deserve scrutiny as possible evidence, but treating them as discrimination regardless of cause goes too far.

consumerism-harmful.reason: Beyond a comfortable level, piling up status goods seems to add little wellbeing and has real environmental costs.

arm-foreign-insurgents.reason: Arming insurgents often backfires and prolongs wars, though helping people resist atrocities can sometimes be justified.

intervene-in-bloc.reason: Invading an ally to keep it in line violates its sovereignty; countries should be free to choose their own alliances and systems.

corporate-influence.reason: Concentrated money buys outsized access in many democracies, though how much it decides outcomes is debated.

restrict-foreign-funding.reason: Transparency rules are reasonable, but restrictions are often used to suppress independent civil society and press.

pronatalist-incentives.reason: Family support has merit on its own, but I don't think it has to be set against immigration as a response to population decline.

residents-only-property.reason: Pressure from second homes can harm communities, but residency restrictions bring their own costs and fairness problems.

job-guarantee.reason: It is an interesting idea with real benefits, but its costs and how well it works at scale are uncertain.

democratic-peace.reason: The democratic peace pattern is fairly well supported, though spreading democracy by force has often gone badly.

no-duty-to-obey.reason: Philosophers seriously dispute this, and I find both the skeptical arguments and the fair-play arguments partly persuasive.

non-intervention.reason: Sovereignty matters a great deal, but an absolute ban would rule out stopping genocide.

industrial-unions.reason: Industrial unions have bargaining advantages, but workers should be free to choose how they organise.

minority-conspiracy.reason: Claims that an ethnic or religious minority secretly plots against the nation are false and have historically fuelled persecution.

abolish-legal-marriage.reason: Legal marriage gives a useful default framework for property, inheritance and care, though I can see the case for decoupling some benefits from it.

public-access-to-information.reason: A legal right to government records is central to accountability, with secrecy reserved for narrow, justified cases.

local-production.reason: Local production has real benefits in places, but trade over long distances often lowers costs and emissions and makes local-by-default a poor general rule.

informal-organisation.reason: Small trust-based groups have their place, but lasting formal organisations are usually what sustain political change over time.

national-law-over-international.reason: International law that a country has agreed to through treaties should generally bind it, even though national courts keep an important role.

religious-nation.reason: Membership in a national community should not depend on religion, and people of every faith or none should belong equally.

deference-to-leading-power.reason: States should deal with each other as formal equals rather than through ritual submission and tribute.

regional-revenue-retention.reason: Some regional autonomy over spending is reasonable, but pooling revenue across regions according to need is part of what makes a shared country work.

personal-possessions-private.reason: Keeping personal belongings private is sensible, but I am not persuaded that all means of production should be held in common, so I am torn on the combined claim.

defeat-communism.reason: Communist states have often been oppressive, but treating their defeat as a goal risks war, and coexistence and competition have usually been the wiser course.

mixed-public-service-providers.reason: A mix of providers within a publicly funded system can work well if quality and access are well regulated, though results vary by service.

religion-illusion.reason: Material hardship plays some role in religious belief, but religion also answers lasting questions of meaning and community that survive prosperity.

capitalism-progressive.reason: Capitalism drove huge gains in productivity and living standards, even though it also brought serious harms and exploitation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.reason: Economic structures like care work and pay matter a great deal for equality, but much progress has come through law and attitudes within existing systems, so I am torn.

socialized-care.reason: Public childcare and similar services are valuable, but replacing family housework and care entirely with public provision goes further than I would want to commit to.

purge-loanwords.reason: Borrowing words is a normal feature of living languages and does not need official purging.

treaties-binding.reason: Treaties with indigenous or other nations are solemn commitments that should not be rewritten unilaterally, though extreme circumstances can complicate this.

cooperative-communities.reason: Cooperative communities are a fine option for those who choose them, but reorganising all of society around them seems neither feasible nor desirable to me.

majority-settlement.reason: State-steered settlement of a majority group into minority regions tends to dilute and marginalise minorities and fuel conflict.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.reason: Pure versions of both have serious problems, but mixed market economies arguably are capitalism, so whether a distinct third way is needed depends on definitions.

historical-land-claim.reason: Historical and religious ties matter, but the rights and claims of people living on a land now should count at least as much.

holocaust-denial.reason: The Holocaust is one of the most thoroughly documented events in history, and it happened as historians describe.

criminalize-homosexuality.reason: Consenting adults should not be punished by law for same-sex relationships.

suppress-opposition.reason: Free opposition and independent organisations are essential protections against abuse of power.

punish-blasphemy.reason: The state should not punish blasphemy or the peaceful practice of any religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.reason: Governing territories mainly to enrich another country exploits their people and is unjust.

defensive-jihad-duty.reason: This is a religious-legal question for Muslims, but I don't think armed resistance should be framed as a universal duty on every believer worldwide.

unreligious-rulers-fought.reason: A government's legitimacy does not rest on enforcing religious law, and using force against rulers on that ground is wrong.

participatory-democracy.reason: People having more direct say in decisions that affect them is valuable, though representative institutions and expertise remain necessary for many decisions.

intersecting-oppressions.reason: Different disadvantages often compound one another, though some problems can still be usefully addressed with targeted measures.

gender-identity-recognition.reason: I support protecting transgender people from discrimination, but how law should handle sex versus gender identity in specific settings is a contested policy question where I'd rather not take a side.

assisted-dying.reason: This is a deep moral disagreement about autonomy, medical ethics and protecting vulnerable people, and I would rather lay out the considerations than take a side.

left-right-obsolete.reason: Left and right still capture real disagreements, but many good policies draw on both and many issues don't fit the axis neatly.

alienated-labor.reason: Much wage work can feel disconnected from creativity, but plenty of work under capitalism is meaningful and alienation is not unique to it.

islam-incompatible.reason: Millions of Muslims live as full participants in Western societies, showing that Islam and Western values can coexist.

divine-source-of-authority.reason: I think political legitimacy is best grounded in the consent of the governed, while respecting that many people see a moral order above it.

religious-dress-in-state.reason: Neutrality of officials has some appeal, but banning religious dress for students and most staff restricts personal freedom more than I think is justified.

ban-nda-harassment.reason: Forced secrecy and arbitration can shield repeat harassers, though victims who prefer confidential settlements should keep that option.

social-market-economy.reason: Markets with competition rules and a social safety net have a strong track record, though the right balance is debatable.

abolish-armed-forces.reason: A few countries manage without armies, but in the current world most countries need some capacity to defend themselves.

rich-first.reason: Uneven early growth has often preceded broad prosperity, provided gains eventually spread and the left-behind are protected.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.reason: Whether neutrality or alliance is safer depends heavily on a country's location and circumstances.

dynastic-succession.reason: Holding real power by inheritance sits poorly with accountability, though ceremonial monarchies with democratic government work fine.

interest-free-mutual-credit.reason: Credit unions and mutuals are valuable, but I don't think for-profit lending should be replaced entirely.

refuse-lender-austerity.reason: Some lender conditions have been harsh and counterproductive, while some reform conditions are reasonable, so it depends on the case.

property-franchise.reason: Every adult citizen should be able to vote regardless of wealth.

domination-women-nature.reason: There are interesting parallels, but I see the oppression of women and environmental exploitation as having largely distinct causes.

reification.reason: Markets can make human-made arrangements feel like natural laws, but they are also genuinely useful coordination tools, so I am torn.

press-owned-by-wealth.reason: Concentrated ownership limits whose voice is heard, but formal press and assembly rights still matter a great deal.

promulgated-standing-laws.reason: Rule by known, general laws applied by independent courts is one of the strongest protections against arbitrary power.

racial-franchise.reason: Tying political rights to race or ethnicity is unjust and denies people equal standing as citizens.

online-participation.reason: Online tools can widen participation, though they need safeguards against manipulation and exclusion of people offline.

open-government-data.reason: Openness about how decisions are made lets citizens hold power to account, with narrow exceptions for privacy and security.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.reason: Whom consenting adults marry is their own choice, and the state has no business policing religious lines.

boycott-minority-shops.reason: Shunning businesses because of their owners' religion is collective discrimination that has historically preceded worse persecution.

citizens-assembly.reason: Deliberative assemblies chosen by lot have worked well on hard questions and are a useful complement to elected bodies.

reinterpret-religion.reason: Traditions that reason about how to apply their teachings in new conditions tend to stay humane, though believers themselves should decide how.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.reason: Extreme concentrations of wealth can translate into outsized political power, though the right remedy is debated.

open-lgbt-military-service.reason: The evidence from many militaries shows open service doesn't harm cohesion, and orientation is irrelevant to doing the job.

state-promotes-atheism.reason: The state should be neutral on religion, and pushing unbelief through schools violates freedom of conscience just as pushing faith would.

abolish-police-prisons.reason: Much policing and incarceration could be replaced by better alternatives, but some capacity to stop and confine violent people is still needed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.reason: In societies emerging from conflict, guaranteed power-sharing has often kept the peace, though it can entrench the divisions it manages.

charity-over-state-aid.reason: Local charity has real strengths, but government programs provide the scale and reliability that poverty relief needs.

term-limits.reason: Term limits curb entrenchment, especially for executives, but for legislators they can shift power to lobbyists and staff.

vote-delegation.reason: Liquid democracy is an interesting idea, but I'm unsure how it would handle concentration of delegated votes and accountability.

existential-risk-priority.reason: Catastrophes that could end humanity deserve serious, funded attention, without crowding out present-day suffering.

women-in-religious-leadership.reason: Who may hold religious office is a question for each faith community, and I'd rather not rule on their internal doctrine.

shared-marital-authority.reason: Spouses are equal partners and should decide together rather than one holding final authority by sex.

foreign-residents-local-vote.reason: Long-term residents pay taxes and use local services, so giving them a voice in local decisions seems fair.

rent-control.reason: Hard rent caps tend to reduce housing supply over time, though limits on sharp increases can protect tenants in the short run.

abolish-ip.reason: Current patent and copyright terms are often too long, but some time-limited protection still helps fund creation and invention.

uniformed-youth.reason: Organizing youth into drilled movements for national ends has a dark history; young people's associations should be voluntary.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.reason: Whether hosting nuclear weapons makes a country safer depends heavily on its situation, and I don't have a general view.

no-foreign-bases.reason: Hosting allied bases by sovereign consent can be a reasonable security choice rather than an inherent loss of sovereignty.

recognise-genocide.reason: Officially acknowledging well-documented genocides matters to survivors and helps prevent denial.

income-for-work-not-ownership.reason: Capital does play a productive role, but I'm sympathetic to the concern that large unearned returns crowd out rewards for work.

never-kill-self-defence.reason: I respect strict pacifism, but lethal force can be a legitimate last resort to protect innocent lives.

unbroken-national-continuity.reason: Nations do draw on old roots, but modern national identities are largely recent constructions that changed a great deal over time.

sex-socially-constructed.reason: Biological sex is a real physical fact, though how societies categorize and interpret it is shaped by culture.

no-fixed-category-of-women.reason: Women do differ greatly, yet shared experiences and interests can still ground collective politics.

martyrs-honoured.reason: Those who die for their country deserve honour, but sacralizing that death can fuel nationalism and future violence.

politics-spiritual-struggle.reason: Treating politics as cosmic good versus evil makes opponents into enemies and compromise impossible.

homeland-cultural-centre.reason: This depends on a particular people's history and wishes, and I don't think there's a general answer.

culture-before-state.reason: Culture and state-building tend to reinforce each other, and I don't see a fixed order that should apply everywhere.

god-not-male.reason: How a faith speaks of God is a theological question for its believers, not one I should take a side on.

scripture-judged-by-women.reason: How believers weigh their sacred texts is an internal religious question I'd rather not adjudicate.

economy-in-majority-hands.reason: Economic roles should be open to everyone; campaigns to take trade away from minorities have repeatedly led to persecution.

single-unit-for-people.reason: Sometimes uniting a people's regions serves self-government well, but borders also need to protect other groups living there.

independent-unions.reason: Unions controlled by the state or a party cannot genuinely represent workers' interests.

socialism-needs-workers-power.reason: That's largely a definitional dispute within socialist thought, and I don't have a strong stake in which definition wins.

local-essentials-public.reason: Natural monopolies like water and core health services are often better kept in public hands, though contracting can work in some cases.

second-chamber.reason: Second chambers can add useful checks and review, but well-functioning unicameral systems exist too.

municipal-property.reason: Municipal ownership suits some utilities, but making it the general rule for all productive property seems unworkable.

confederal-coordination.reason: Larger-scale problems like climate or infrastructure often need joint bodies that can make binding decisions.

family-wage.reason: Families need adequate income, but I think that's better secured through a mix of wages and support like child benefits than by tying pay to household size.

ageing-research-funding.reason: Ageing drives most disease, so research into slowing it could greatly reduce suffering, as long as it doesn't crowd out other health needs.

anonymous-payments.reason: Financial privacy matters for freedom, but some ability to trace payments is needed against fraud, extortion and serious crime.

online-anonymity.reason: Pseudonymity protects dissidents, vulnerable people and honest speech, even though it is sometimes abused.

person-over-state.reason: Each person has a dignity that the state exists to protect, not to spend for collective goals.

spiritual-nature.reason: People clearly need meaning and belonging beyond material goods, though I'm wary of the state defining what spiritual flourishing is.

regional-powers-revocable.reason: Both parliamentary supremacy and entrenched federal guarantees can work well, and which fits depends on the country's history.

gm-crops.reason: The evidence on safety is strong and the yield and pesticide benefits are real, with sensible regulation of specific traits.

dense-cities.reason: Per person, compact cities generally use less energy and land, though density alone doesn't guarantee good outcomes.

racial-group-interests.reason: Groups facing discrimination can reasonably organise, but treating race as the basis of distinct political interests tends to entrench division.

racial-pride.reason: Pride in heritage and ancestry is harmless and often valuable, but pride in race as such slides easily into supremacism.

defensive-wars-only.reason: Self-defence is the clearest justification, but defending allies or stopping genocide can also justify force.

language-defines-nation.reason: Shared language and history matter, but nationhood also depends on people's own sense of belonging and political will.

communal-electorates.reason: Separate religious electorates harden communal divisions and undercut common citizenship.

foreign-partition-plot.reason: As an AI I don't have a country of my own, so the statement doesn't apply to me.

free-public-college.reason: Free tuition widens access but often subsidises better-off students, and targeted aid can do more for those who need it.

pollution-taxes.reason: Pricing pollution is usually the most efficient tool, though regulation and public investment remain necessary alongside it.

future-generations.reason: We have a real duty not to leave people who come after us a degraded planet.

women-distinct-values.reason: Values vary widely among women and men, and weighting views by gender rests on generalisations I'm wary of.

arms-reduction.reason: Keeping arms at the minimum needed for security reduces the risk and cost of conflict, though what is minimal is hard to judge.

open-diplomacy.reason: Binding treaties should be public, but negotiations often need confidentiality to succeed.

capital-controls.reason: Free capital movement is generally beneficial, though temporary controls can be a sensible tool in a crisis.

state-arms-monopoly.reason: A state monopoly on organised force is a foundation of rule of law, though resistance to tyrannical regimes is a hard exception.

soldiers-refuse-war.reason: Soldiers should refuse clearly unlawful orders, but a blanket duty to refuse every interstate war goes too far.

collective-bargaining.reason: Collective bargaining corrects power imbalances, but making it the only way terms are set is too rigid for every sector.

in-work-tax-credits.reason: Topping up low earnings through the tax system supports work and reduces poverty fairly efficiently.

fiscal-rules-binding.reason: Fiscal rules can build credibility, but rigid legal limits can force harmful austerity in recessions.

restructure-world-economy.reason: Some trade, debt and finance rules do disadvantage poorer countries and could be made fairer.

smash-state-machine.reason: Destroying existing institutions wholesale has a terrible historical record compared with reforming them.

free-economic-experiment.reason: Letting communities try different arrangements within a free society is a good way to learn what works.

nature-as-capital.reason: Counting natural depletion as a cost improves decisions, even if not everything about nature's worth can be priced.

sacred-nation.reason: Nations can give real meaning to people, but treating them as sacred tends to justify sacrificing individuals to them.

student-debt-relief.reason: Relief helps struggling borrowers but broad cancellation is poorly targeted, so I'd favour targeted relief and reform.

internal-colonialism.reason: Central regions can extract resources and wealth from peripheral ones in ways that resemble colonial patterns, though the analogy has limits.

shared-human-nature.reason: I think there is a shared human nature that grounds dignity, but I'm not sure every modification of it is wrong.

public-service-media.reason: Independent public broadcasters can strengthen the information ecosystem when their independence is well protected.

religions-one-truth.reason: This is a theological question on which I don't think it's my place to take a side.

farm-price-support.reason: Farmers need protection from volatility and predatory lending, but guaranteed prices often distort markets and favour large producers.

keep-nuclear-weapons.reason: Unilateral disarmament while rivals stay armed could reduce stability, so multilateral reduction seems the safer path.

workers-own-party.reason: Workers can be well represented either by their own parties or within broad ones, depending on the political system.

women-property-inheritance.reason: Equal rights to inherit and own land are a basic matter of equality before the law.

one-language-many-names.reason: The line between language and dialect is partly political, so regions' own naming deserves weight alongside linguistic criteria.

pollution-tort-liability.reason: Liability is valuable, but diffuse pollution harming many people is poorly handled by lawsuits alone, so agencies are needed too.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.reason: An advisory role can respect custom and local legitimacy, as long as it doesn't override elected representatives or individual rights.

environment-over-liberty.reason: Some limits on freedom to prevent environmental harm are justified, but a general priority over liberty is too sweeping.

mandatory-sentences.reason: Mandatory minimums have often produced unjust outcomes, and judges are better placed to weigh individual cases.

immigrants-learn-language.reason: Learning the language is very valuable and should be well supported, but hard requirements can be unfair to some, such as elderly migrants.

no-compulsory-union.reason: There's a real tension between individual freedom of association and the free-rider problem for unions that represent everyone.

voter-id.reason: ID can be reasonable if it's free and easy to obtain, but documentation requirements can exclude eligible voters and in-person fraud is rare.

religious-equal-recognition.reason: The state should not pick winners among interpretations of a faith, though many countries have established churches that work tolerably.

democracy-is-procedure.reason: Fair elections are essential, but they depend on rights like free speech and press, so democracy needs more than the vote itself.

premarital-sex.reason: Consenting adult women should be free to make their own sexual choices without legal or social punishment.

internet-shutdowns.reason: Shutdowns are usually disproportionate and often used to suppress dissent, though I can't rule out every extreme emergency.

negative-income-tax.reason: A unified cash payment is simpler and respects choice, but some needs, like disability or housing, may still require targeted programs.

women-suffrage.reason: Women should have exactly the same political rights as men.

religion-oppresses-women.reason: Religious institutions have often entrenched patriarchy, but they have also been vehicles for women's agency, and economic and legal structures matter at least as much.

race-social-construct.reason: Racial categories track some ancestry-linked variation, but their boundaries and meaning are largely socially drawn rather than natural divisions.

gender-equality-agencies.reason: Such bodies can help or become symbolic; whether they are worth it depends on the country and how they are run.

homestead-ownership.reason: First labour gives a real claim, but I doubt it alone settles full ownership of scarce resources others also need.

international-criminal-courts.reason: Atrocities and aggression are often committed by the very people who control domestic courts, so an international venue is needed for accountability.

scripture-inerrant.reason: I read scripture as a deeply important human-mediated tradition, and strict literalism fits poorly with its genres and history.

gendered-self-government.reason: Basic equality for women seems a fair floor for any self-government, though how it is built in should respect local institutions.

defend-planned-state.reason: I would not treat an economic system as worth defending apart from whether the state respects the people living under it.

indirect-election.reason: Direct election generally gives voters clearer accountability than tiered delegate systems.

national-church-status.reason: Equal legal standing for all religions seems fairer, though mild ceremonial establishments can coexist with real freedom.

minority-territorial-autonomy.reason: Territorial autonomy has often reduced conflict and protected minorities, though it is not right in every case.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.reason: The wishes of the people who live there should weigh heavily, even if a vote cannot settle every case alone.

keep-colonial-borders.reason: Arbitrary as they are, keeping inherited borders has on balance prevented more wars than redrawing them would have.

simple-living.reason: Moderation has real merits, but trade and abundance have lifted billions out of poverty and self-sufficiency is not a general ideal for me.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.reason: I am torn between protecting vulnerable indigenous communities and the general freedom of citizens to move within their country.

equal-conscription.reason: If a state compels service, applying it to men only is hard to justify on equality grounds.

homeland-spiritual-bond.reason: Attachment to ancestral land is meaningful for many people, but I would not make it a binding spiritual duty of a nation.

extrajudicial-killing.reason: Killing suspects without trial abandons due process and has led to many innocent deaths.

close-ties-china.reason: This depends heavily on each country's situation and is a live geopolitical choice I would rather not take a side on.

protect-kin-minorities.reason: Cultural support for co-ethnics abroad can be benign, but it is also a common pretext for meddling in neighbours' affairs.

resources-common-ownership.reason: Land and natural resources are not made by anyone, so the idea that appropriators owe others something for them is persuasive to me.

self-ownership.reason: Strong rights over one's body are important, though I would not treat them as absolutely excluding all shared obligations such as taxes.

cut-consumption-tax.reason: Consumption taxes are efficient but regressive, and exemptions or rebates can address the burden on necessities without abolishing them.

targeted-social-spending.reason: Targeting stretches money further, while universal programs gain wider support and avoid benefit cliffs; good systems mix both.

bypass-parties-groups.reason: Parties and organised groups are essential intermediaries, and bypassing them tends to concentrate power in a single leader.

no-business-privileges.reason: Favouring well-connected firms is cronyism that distorts markets and corrupts government.

no-denominational-politics.reason: Cross-cutting parties tend to be healthier, though confessional power-sharing has sometimes been a necessary peace deal.

tech-with-ancestral-values.reason: Some continuity with tradition can sit well with technology, but the archaic-revivalist version of this idea gives me pause.

wife-divorce-without-consent.reason: No one should be held in a marriage by another person's veto.

national-resource-control.reason: National control can secure fair returns but often leads to mismanagement, and good contracts with foreign firms can serve a country well.

distribution-by-process.reason: How wealth was gained matters a lot, but I think extreme outcomes can be unjust even when each step was voluntary.

financial-transactions-tax.reason: Economists genuinely disagree on whether such a tax curbs harmful speculation or just shifts trading and raises costs.

racism-not-main-obstacle.reason: This is an empirically disputed and politically charged question where I would rather present the evidence than take a side.

unjust-law-not-binding.reason: Severe injustice can defeat a law's moral claim on us, though for ordinary flawed laws reform is usually the better path.

automate-paid-work.reason: Freeing people from unwanted toil is good if the gains are widely shared, though meaningful work should remain available.

multipolar-world.reason: Balances of power can check domination but can also be unstable; strong rules-based institutions matter more to me than the number of poles.

labour-theory-of-value.reason: Labour matters a great deal, but prices and value also reflect demand, scarcity and other inputs.

patriotism-serves-workers.reason: An inclusive civic patriotism and solidarity with working people can reinforce each other rather than conflict.

material-over-identity.reason: This is an internal strategic debate for the left that I would rather not weigh in on.

market-under-party-rule.reason: China shows markets can grow under communist party rule, but whether the result is still socialist is debatable.
